concern_details.detail: main architectural components and their responsibilities
concern_details.why: Six components match the code's structure: Boundary GUIs, Control controllers, ReportService/UserService, the JPA entities and state classes, Database (PersistenceService/JpaUtil) and MySQL reports_db. Each box now has a one-line responsibility, and the responsibilities hold up against the code. PersistenceService does generic save/update/find with EntityTransaction. The services return Map data. SystemServicesController creates and fronts the use-case controllers, while UserLoginGUI uses UserLoginController directly, hence 'mostly via'.

The four layers (presentation, application, domain, persistence) appear as one component each, and each label names its code package (Boundary, Control, Entity, Database). The services and entities boxes both say 'package Entity', so the reader can see that the code's Entity package holds both. Grouping the boxes in UML packages would be more explicit, but the labels are enough at overview level.

The imports confirm every drawn dependency. Boundary imports Control (SystemServicesController and UserLoginController) and Entity.ReportCategory (ReportCreationGUI, ReceivedReportsGUI). Control imports only ReportService/UserService, apart from an unused ReportCategory import. The services import Database.PersistenceService and use entity classes. persistence.xml maps the entities and points at jdbc:mysql .../reports_db. The view draws no extra layer-skipping edges and leaves none out.

concern_details.detail: separation of user interface, application logic, domain entities and persistence, and how they collaborate
concern_details.why: The diagram shows that the UI and controllers never touch persistence and that only the services and persistence touch the entities. The UI reaches the entities only for the category enum. 'Return Map-based data' on the services box tells the reader that entity objects do not flow up to the controllers, and the code confirms this.

level_why: The perspective asks for an overview: one component per layer, 6 components plus one actor and 8 relations. The diagram has no individual screens, controllers or classes, so nothing needs to be cut. The only class name in a box is SystemServicesController, which is acceptable because it names the facade that defines how the UI enters the application layer. Adding the individual controllers or UML layer packages would take the view past the overview level.
uml: Minor: the external MySQL database is drawn as a component and marked external only by the '(external)' text. A component is acceptable in a component diagram, but an explicit system boundary (for example a <<subsystem>> around the five application components) would make inside and outside clear in standard notation. Optional at this level.

Minor: persistence ..> entities rests on the persistence.xml mapping, not on an import (PersistenceService is generic in <T>). It is a valid UML dependency. Its label 'maps to tables' is fine; a <<use>> keyword is optional.
fixes: Optional: enclose the five in-process components in one <<subsystem>> (or a system boundary) so the external MySQL database sits visibly outside it, without adding layer packages.
